newsitem.title: SPAIN: Tabacalera 9-mth net seen down 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Tabacalera 9-mth net seen down 10 pct.

text.p: Spanish tobacco firm Tabacalera should see a 10 percent decline in its nine-month net profit to 8.39 billion pesetas, dented by the impact of the July tax hike on tobacco, analysts said on Wednesday.
The company, 52-percent owned by the Spanish State, will announce its nine month results later this week.
"The rise in taxes on Virginia tobacco brought a net loss of income of around 2.36 billion pesetas," said Alfredo Echevarria, analyst at Benito y Monjardin brokerage.
An analyst at Ahorro Corporacion said: "We ascribe the fall (in net attributable profit) to the decline in operating margin after the government hiked taxes last August."
In July this year Spanish government, eager to cover a huge shortfall in the 1995 budget, raised "sin-taxes" on cigarettes and alcohol.
In response Tabacalera increased the prices in its black tobacco but absorbed the price rise on Virginia, or blond, tobacco, which is more open to international competition.

Tabacalera shares were hard hit by the news and fell sharply. On Wednesday at 1300 GMT they were trading at 4,680 pesetas, down 20 pesetas from yesterday and almost 30 percent lower than on July 25, before news of the hike.
Analysts were not ruling out the possibility that major brands will eventually raise prices on Virginia cigarettes in order to recover at least part of their operating margins.
One analyst mentioned that Tabacalera could compensate a lower operating margin with extraordinary results.
Another said the company could count on 1.01 billion pesetas, which appear under "variation in provisions", to offset lower profits this year.
Another question mark over the firm's future was the allocation of a stake in Portugal's Tabaqueira.
Tabacalera is currently bidding for 65 percent of Tabaquiera but the Portuguese government has yet to announce who will be awarded the first tranche in the privatisation.
